newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-SPAIN'S MOYA ROCKETS INTO TOP 10.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SPAIN'S MOYA ROCKETS INTO TOP 10.

text.p: Win or lose Sunday's Australian Open final against Pete Sampras, Spanish giant-killer Carlos Moya has earned a place in the top 10 of men's tennis, officials said on Friday.
Moya, ranked 25th and with just one singles title to his name at the start of the event, will soar to the world number six spot if he beats top seed Sampras.
If he loses, he will become world number nine in the next official rankings, to be released on Monday.
Moya's leap into the top 10 caps a stunning rise through the rankings since 1994, when he finished the year ranked 346.

The unseeded Spaniard has claimed two of the game's best players at the Australian Open, ousting defending champion Boris Becker in a stunning first-round upset and then overwhelming second seed Michael Chang in a semifinal on Thursday.
The scattering of the top seeds over the past two weeks at Melbourne Park has reshuffled the world rankings, though Sampras keeps the top ranking even if he is beaten on Sunday.
Becker however has paid dearly for his early exit, and will drop out of the top 10 no matter who lifts the cup here on Sunday. He came into the tournament ranked six.
Chang's ranking will sink to four whoever wins on Sunday after he finished last year as number two, the highest year-end ranking of his career.
Croat Goran Ivanisevic, who reached the quarter-finals here, will replace Chang as number two. Austrian Thomas Muster, who on Friday lost his semifinal against Sampras, jumps to three.
